fragments.text: Can I tail the callgrind log?

reply_text:
㊥ (tailing callgrind) There's nothing running to tail. Both callgrind runs have already finished, and quickly. The empty file took 6 s under valgrind (23:19:37–43), and `import Lean` took 12 s (23:19:58–23:20:10). Their bg.py logs are `/tmp/futon3c-bg/bg-1790810377973-40.log` and `bg-1790810398922-41.log`, and the raw profiles are `/tmp/envtrace-{empty,import}.cg` and `.cg.1`. So the two-hour limit never came into play. The follow-up job I queued should just come back with "already complete".

㊢ (what codex-5 is doing now) codex-5 is correcting how the runs are split, not rerunning them. It split each run where Lean marks the end of initialization (`lean_io_mark_end_initialization`). The second half then also included shutdown code, so it's narrowing "after initialization" to the time spent inside `Lean.Elab.runFrontend`. Its draft table is in `/tmp/envinit-trace-summary.txt`, and its built-in check passes: the parser runs after initialization, and a grind propagator runs only during initialization.

㊟ (draft numbers) I'm not quoting the draft numbers yet. The row totals don't add up to the class sizes I know (the parse row sums to 838 against 829), so I don't yet know what each column means. I'll report the numbers once codex-5 commits and I've reviewed them.

previous_reply_acts.text: (the 2-hour limit) I can't get the lifted limit to codex-5 while its current job runs, because Agency has no way to message a job in progress. So I've queued a follow-up job that starts as soon as the trace finishes. If the `import Lean` run was cut for time, codex-5 then runs it under `bg.py` with no time limit. If it was already done, codex-5 just confirms. The follow-up is `invoke-1790810368270-29383-b2d13ada`, parked as `park-c8ccb385…` with a 5-hour deadline.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (current trace) The first job, `…29381-d0a50e6b`, is running, and its last activity was at 23:19. Its own park (`park-552926e7…`) still wakes me when it reports back, so I'll report the empty-file numbers then, before the longer run finishes.
